Then, calculate the discriminant (Δ = b² - 4ac). If Δ > 0, there are two real and distinct roots. If Δ = 0, there is one real root. If Δ < 0, there are no real roots. Finally, use the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a) to find the roots.

To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Then, set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x to find the critical points. Next, find the second derivative of the function, f''(x). Finally, evaluate the second derivative at each critical point. If f''(x) > 0, the function has a local minimum at that point. If f''(x) < 0, the function has a local maximum at that point.
